key_insight: Independent multi-agent reinforcement learning can coordinate large EV fleets to reduce charging cost while mitigating grid congestion without requiring direct communication between vehicles.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical framework for decentralized EV charging control that can support distribution-network stability under dynamic pricing and high penetration of electrified transport.
method: Compared contextual combinatorial bandits and policy-gradient agents for decentralized charging decisions.
Agents used only local information such as price signals, state of charge, and time constraints.
Evaluated mixed-strategy and heterogeneous fleets under different congestion conditions in simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation in a realistic simulation environment using dynamic electricity pricing derived from real photovoltaic production data across varying congestion levels.
watch_item: Performance is shown in simulation, so real-world deployment may face gaps in forecast accuracy, user behavior, and grid-model fidelity.
paper_title: Smart charging of large fleets of Electric Vehicles: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches
